rows.scope: Apply mathematics to problems in everyday life, society and workplace.
Use a problem-solving model: analyze, plan, solve, justify, and evaluate reasonableness.
Select tools and techniques including objects, manipulatives, technology, mental mathematics, estimation and number sense.
Communicate reasoning through symbols, diagrams, graphs and language.
Create representations to organize, record and communicate mathematical ideas.
Analyze mathematical relationships to connect and communicate ideas.
Explain and justify arguments using precise written or oral mathematical language.
Recognize quantities of structured arrangements instantly.
Compose and decompose numbers up to 120 with concrete/pictorial models in hundreds, tens and ones in more than one way.
Represent numbers up to 120 using objects, pictures, expanded and standard forms.
Generate numbers greater or less than a given whole number up to 120.
Compare whole numbers up to 120 using place value and comparative language.
Order whole numbers up to 120 using place value and open number lines.
Compare two numbers up to 100 with >, <, or = symbols.
Use concrete and pictorial models to find the sum of a multiple of ten and a one-digit number in problems up to 99.
Solve joining, separating and comparing word problems within 20, allowing unknowns in any term.
Compose ten with two or more addends, with and without objects.
Apply addition/subtraction fact strategies within 20, including making ten and decomposing to ten.
Explain addition/subtraction strategies through words, models and number sentences for problems up to 20.
Generate and solve situations from given addition/subtraction number sentences within 20.
